detail: ticket 2: first merge passed, 0 merge failure(s), 10 steps; recall showed 5 fact(s)

memories_after: [Fact] The docs project runs on the coding@1 report template with main branch main and marks work done via submit_report, which returns a commit hash. Its agenium.toml declares key_prefix AGN, main_branch main, template coding@1, empty shared_dirs/include_files, an empty pre_merge check and an empty network allowlist.
[Fact] In the docs project, agents can verify a file's exact bytes with PowerShell [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes to confirm LF endings, no BOM and no trailing whitespace before submitting.

[Lesson] When the docs pre-merge check rejects a file for a missing required header line, prepend that line (e.g. 'Owner: docs-team') as line 1 and keep the ticket's required content below it — this passed both the AC and the check.

[Lesson] Before submitting a report on a docs/deliverables ticket, check the file against all project conventions (e.g. the required 'Owner: docs-team' first line), since acceptance-criteria checks and an approving review can pass while the pre-merge check still fails at merge time.
[Fact] In the docs project, team documents live in the deliverables/ and reports/ directories, as stated in the project README.
[Fact] In this environment shell commands run in PowerShell on Windows, so Get-Content and Select-String are used for file verification.
[Fact] In the docs project, ticket work is done on branch agenium/<ticket-id> in a git worktree under projects/docs/.agenium/worktrees/<ticket-id>.
[Fact] In the docs project, every team document in deliverables/ or reports/ must have its first line exactly 'Owner: docs-team' (project rule enforced by a pre-merge check).
